title: Macro Defect Inspection - Micro-cracks Detection on Puma 9xxx
subtitle: Post-Lithography Quality Validation for 65nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Sarah Chen

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Puma 9xxx system to detect and classify Micro-cracks defects during post-lithography inspection at the 65nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab B to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Micro-cracks defects that are critical to yield at the 65nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Puma 9xxx platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Puma 9xxx
- Inspection Type: Macro Defect Inspection
- Target Defect: Micro-cracks
- Process Step: Post-Lithography
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 65nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab B

This test case applies to all Puma 9xxx systems deployed at Milpitas Fab B for post-lithography monitoring in the 65nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Puma 9xxx
Software Version: v11.2.233
Recipe: MACRO_DEFECT_INSPECTION_65nm_POST_LITHOGRAPHY
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: High (121 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 3mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Puma 9xxx system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Macro Defect Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Micro-cracks defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 65nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 103 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 94% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.5% for Macro Defect Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.93 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-04-26
Wafers Tested: 41
Total Defects Found: 4817
Defect Density: 1533.3 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 7.0%
Capture Rate: 95.6%
Test Duration: 342 minutes
System Uptime: 98.1%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Puma 9xxx demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Micro-cracks at the 65nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Throughput metrics met production requirements without sensitivity compromise.

e) Recipe portability between systems at this fab was confirmed.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
